actions.label: Investigate: Preserve autocomplete selection during accent replacement

reproduce.title: duplicate quick accent characters in web browser address bar
reproduce.version_requirement: Reported version and current supported build
prerequisites: Quick Accent is enabled with the reporter activation setting.
reproduce.expected_result: Only the intended d and accented u remain, with no extra unaccented u or selected suffix.
steps: Type d into the address bar so Edge selects its autocomplete suffix.
Enter accented u through Quick Accent and record resulting text/selection.
Repeat in a plain text field and with autocomplete disabled; compare character counts and selection transitions.

known_information: Typing d in an Edge address bar can select the remainder of a history suggestion such as duckduckgo.com.
Entering an accented u then yields duu-with-an-accent instead of d followed by the accented character.
The original diagnostic archive and reproduction already exist, and a later report says the behavior persists.
initial_investigation: Read the complete issue body and public discussion, current ownership, labels and linked-work history.
Read the expected-versus-actual address-bar example and subsequent confirmation.
Quick Accent sends replacement input through its keyboard service; the existing architecture separates hook state, toolbar UI and input injection.
inferences: Quick Accent replacement/backspace input may operate on a changing autocomplete selection rather than only the physical base character.
issue_context.summary: Quick Accent replacement interacts incorrectly with the selected autocomplete suffix in Edge.
issue_context.analysis: The browser scenario is concrete. Maintainer reproduction with the selected suffix is more useful than another report request, and the selection transition must be observed before changing input injection.

fix_assessment.rationale: This is a scoped, confidence-qualified investigation/fix proposal, not an approved or independently converged implementation design.

judgment.rationale: The browser scenario is concrete. Maintainer reproduction with the selected suffix is more useful than another report request, and the selection transition must be observed before changing input injection.
judgment.recommended_action: Reproduce with an active selected autocomplete suffix and compare with a plain text control before choosing the replacement boundary.

title: duplicate quick accent characters in web browser address bar

confidence.rationale: The maintainer-reproducible selection scenario localizes the interaction, but no injection trace proves its exact ordering.

plan: Create the reported Edge history suggestion and record selection state before and after Quick Accent activation.
Compare the replacement sequence against a plain TextBox and Edge with autocomplete disabled.
Adjust only the proven base-character replacement/injection ordering and add a regression for selected suffixes without deleting unrelated text.
proposed_fixes.title: Preserve autocomplete selection during accent replacement
proposed_fixes.root_cause: The injected replacement sequence may race or mis-handle the browser selected-suffix transition; the exact ordering remains unconfirmed.
verification: d plus accented u becomes exactly the intended two characters with no duplicate base character.
Verify ordinary text fields, combining accents, and cancellation preserve existing text.
